column1: # Hungarian (hu) catalog. Same format as zh-hant.tsv:  context <TAB> source <TAB> translation
# (empty context = a plain UI string; `@id` = a command id; `@plural` = "one|other" source, and a
# single translated form: Hungarian uses the singular after a number, see `plural_none`).
# Clean-room: every entry was written from the meaning of VectorCraft's English label, using the
# general Hungarian vocabulary of vector illustration (rajztábla, útvonal, horgonypont, fogantyú,
# körvonal, kitöltés, színátmenet, színminta, mintázat, réteg, vágómaszk, átlátszatlanság,
# keverési mód, összemosás, Útvonalkezelő, előbeállítás, effektus). No proprietary localisation
# resource, string table or product UI was consulted or copied; add entries the same way.
# Conventions: the user is addressed informally (te); menu commands are nouns of action (Mentés,
# Megnyitás, Rács megjelenítése), dialog buttons short verbs (Alkalmaz, Visszaállít, Bezár; the
# File menu's Close keeps its noun through an `@id` row); tool names drop the word "tool" (Toll,
# Közvetlen kijelölés); only the first word of a label is capitalised. No case suffix or article
# is attached to a placeholder: the sentence puts it after a colon instead ("Mentve: {path}").
# Quotation marks are „ ”, the dash is –, prose uses the decimal comma. Key names stay as the menus
# show shortcuts (Ctrl, Shift, Alt, Esc). Status and error messages keep the case of their
# English first word, as they are often shown after "…: ".
# Coverage: the whole interface (every menu string and `tl!` literal, `complete_menus`) and the
# status and error messages (`COMPLETE_MESSAGES`), gaps listed by `untranslated_report`. Left in English on
# purpose (`MENU_KEEP_AS_IS`): the product name, language names, OpenType, the built-in workspace
# names and the bracketed perspective grid preset names; `hu-HU` and every other `hu-*` locale
